newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila C. Bank sells $20-$30 mln at 26.379 pesos.
newsitem.headline: Manila C. Bank sells $20-$30 mln at 26.379 pesos.

text.p: The Philippine Central Bank sold about $20 million to $30 million early on Thursday in order to calm the Philippine peso/U.S. dollar market due to the renewed weakness in the Thai baht, traders said.
The expected resignation of Thai finance minister Amnuay Viravan is causing pressure on the Thai baht, traders said.
"The market is nervous. There is the possibility of another attack on the peso due to the Thai baht," a dealer said.
In May, the Philippine peso was hit by the backlash from the Thai baht's problems, prompting the Central Bank to raise its key rate to a two-year high of 20 percent.
Since then, the Central Bank had slowly cut its overnight borrowing rate which now stands at 12.75 percent.
